title: Probabilistic schema fallback test harness for FP8/INT8 function-call outputs
creator: Aria Patel
summary: Build a test harness that exercises FP8/INT8 model variants with probabilistic schema fallback and token-level confidence stamps to measure end-to-end function-call JSON adherence under realistic traffic patterns.
background: Recent regressions in structured outputs after low-bit calibration surfaced intermittent schema violations in function calls. Existing testbeds focus on strict pass/fail; we need probabilistic controls to quantify partial failures and design fallback/repair policies.
goals: 1) Quantify schema adherence drop-rate and severity across FP8/INT8 profiles. 2) Validate probabilistic fallback heuristics that repair incomplete JSON or route to higher-precision variants. 3) Produce a signal surface for console alerts and rollout policies.
success_metrics: 1) False-negative schema violation rate <= 0.5% for P0 endpoints after fallback. 2) Mean time to repair (auto-repair or fallback) <= 200ms. 3) Detectable correlation between calibration stats and schema failure (>0.6 Pearson).
approach: Create a harness that runs parallelized prompts with synthetic perturbations, prompt shuffling, and real customer prompt seeds. Attach token-level confidence estimates and KV-cache replay to reproduce failures. Implement a probabilistic fallback layer that triggers based on schema-likelihood and confidence decay.
test_plan: 1) Dataset: 3k canonical function-call prompts + 10k fuzzed variants. 2) Models: reference FP16, INT8-quantized, FP8-dynquant. 3) Metrics: schema-pass, parse-errors, field-mismatch, extraneous-keys, runtime-to-repair. 4) Run nightly against staging dedicated pool with canary routing enabled.
observations: Initial run (2026-03-04): INT8 shows 1.8% parse-errors on nested objects; FP8 shows 2.3% but with different error profiles.
Token-confidence heuristics reduce parse-errors by ~45% when threshold tuned per-schema.
KV-cache replay reproduces ~70% of intermittent failures — indicates batch scheduling influence.
blockers: Need deterministic replay for dynamic batching (infra ticket ENG-67921).
Calibration telemetry currently samples 10% of traffic; need full metrics for correlation analysis.
decisions: Use probabilistic fallback that prefers structured-repair heuristics over immediate rollback to FP16 for low-severity parse errors.
Expose a schema-failure score in console at per-route granularity to drive rollout policies.
next_steps: Wire harness into CI pipeline and add Slack alerting channel.
Prototype auto-repair library with 3 heuristics: closing-bracket insertion, field-type coercion, and guided re-query.
Sync with Calibration team to increase telemetry sampling; follow up with ENG-67921 and ENG-68002.
